description: Add the caller-agnostic DocumentCache materializer contract in the backend layer. Define an IDocumentCacheMaterializer-style service, request model, success candidate model, typed ordinary outcomes, deterministic projection-processing exceptions for invariant failures, and target-fatal mapping failure classification for unsafe target context defects. The request should carry the resolved target context inputs available from earlier work, the DocumentId, an optional selected durable-work RequiredContentVersion for diagnostics only, a materialization purpose, and a cancellation token. The contract must not resolve targets, inspect lifecycle, page or delete durable work, write DocumentCache, shape Kafka envelopes, authorize requests, or apply readable profiles.
acceptance-criteria: The materializer request identifies a document by internal DocumentId and never by public DocumentUuid lookup.
The optional selected durable-work RequiredContentVersion is available only as worker-local diagnostic context and is not returned as current source evidence.

A success candidate contains DocumentId, DocumentUuid, ProjectName, ResourceName, ResourceVersion, current ContentVersion, current LastModifiedAt from ContentLastModifiedAt, StreamEtag, and DocumentJson.
The success candidate does not contain ComputedAt, cache-write decisions, caught-up decisions, authorization decisions, or lifecycle decisions.
Ordinary non-success outcomes are limited to missing canonical source and source changed during hydration.
Invariant failures throw deterministic projection-processing exceptions with bounded reason codes and sanitized metadata.
Target/mapping defects surface as target-fatal failures rather than per-document materialization outcomes.
Cancellation, transient database failures, and provider/runtime failures follow the existing exception flow and are not converted into cache candidates.
steps-to-verify: Review the new contract types and confirm the request/result surface matches reference/design/backend-redesign/epics/18-document-cache/02-document-materializer-service.md.

description: Add a first-class cache-projection read/materialization mode for ordinary relational resources. Extend the existing relational read materializer and supporting contracts so callers can request the caller-agnostic cache projection directly instead of post-processing ExternalResponse or StoredDocument output. The cache mode should reuse compiled ResourceReadPlan hydration, compiled reconstitution, descriptor URI projection, and document-reference lookup link emission.
acceptance-criteria: Cache projection emits a JSON object with top-level id and _lastModifiedDate.
Cache projection never emits _etag in DocumentJson.
Cache projection bypasses readable-profile projection and is independent of request authorization context.
Ordinary resource cache projection uses the fixed link-bearing stream representation whenever the read plan has document references, regardless of ResourceLinks:Enabled.
The implementation does not use string surgery over an external API response, trigger-side JSON construction, provider-specific JSON composition SQL, or Newtonsoft.Json.
Existing StoredDocument and ExternalResponse materialization behavior remains unchanged for current callers.
steps-to-verify: Inspect the implementation to confirm it uses System.Text.Json/JsonNode/Utf8JsonWriter-style APIs rather than raw response string edits.

description: Add descriptor support for the cache-projection materialization mode. Reuse the existing descriptor read row and descriptor materialization rules while producing the cache-owned document shape: id and _lastModifiedDate included, _etag omitted, no readable profile projection, and no link-bearing stream behavior for descriptors.
acceptance-criteria: Descriptor cache projection emits namespace, codeValue, shortDescription, optional descriptor fields, id, and _lastModifiedDate.
Descriptor cache projection never emits _etag.
Descriptor cache projection uses the descriptor no-link stream context for StreamEtag composition.
Descriptor cache projection does not run namespace authorization or readable-profile projection.
Existing descriptor GET/query external response and stored-document behavior remains unchanged.

description: Integrate fixed stream ETag composition into the materializer. Use the shared served-ETag composer with current ContentVersion, the selected effective-schema hash, JSON format, no readable profile, identity content coding, and the fixed stream link mode. Ordinary resources use the link-bearing context; descriptors use the descriptor no-link context. Return StreamEtag separately from DocumentJson.
acceptance-criteria: StreamEtag is composed with IServedEtagComposer or the local shared served-ETag composition helper rather than a duplicate formatter.
Ordinary resource StreamEtag uses profile null, ResponseFormat.Json, identity content coding, and link flag true.
Descriptor StreamEtag uses profile null, ResponseFormat.Json, identity content coding, and link flag false.
ResourceLinks:Enabled does not affect cache StreamEtag composition.
DocumentJson remains free of _etag while StreamEtag is returned as a separate candidate field.
steps-to-verify: Review code paths for ResourceLinksOptions usage and confirm it does not influence cache StreamEtag.

description: Implement the source metadata reader used by the materializer. The reader should load the current canonical dms.Document row by DocumentId and join or resolve immutable dms.ResourceKey metadata needed to select the compiled mapping/read plan and denormalized cache fields. It should return missing-source when the canonical document row is absent and surface a target-fatal mapping failure when the selected target mapping set cannot safely resolve the ResourceKeyId or read path.
acceptance-criteria: The reader queries canonical source metadata by DocumentId.
The first source observation includes DocumentId, DocumentUuid, ResourceKeyId, ContentVersion, ContentLastModifiedAt, ProjectName, ResourceName, and ResourceVersion.
A missing dms.Document row is represented as the materializer's missing-source outcome.

A ResourceKeyId missing from the selected mapping set, a missing read plan, or a missing descriptor materialization path is treated as a target-fatal mapping failure rather than an ordinary per-document outcome.
The reader does not query DocumentProjectionWork, DocumentCache, ContentVersion ranges, or public DocumentUuid lookup.

Inspect SQL or command builders to confirm DocumentProjectionWork and DocumentCache are not read by this component.

description: Implement ordinary resource hydration inside the DocumentCache materializer. After source metadata and read-plan selection, hydrate the single document by DocumentId using the existing IDocumentHydrator/PageKeysetSpec.Single flow, single-document fast path, descriptor URI projection, and document-reference lookup needed for fixed link-bearing cache output. The implementation should use ordinary target read semantics and must not take work-row locks or deliberate write-conflicting source-row locks.
acceptance-criteria: Ordinary resources hydrate from canonical relational tables selected by DocumentId.
Hydration uses the compiled read plan for the resource resolved from ResourceKeyId.
Document-reference lookup is included when the plan supports link emission for the cache projection.
Descriptor URI projection remains available for descriptor-valued fields in ordinary resources.
Hydration uses ordinary target read semantics and does not opt into explicit snapshot, serializable, work-row lock, or source-row update-lock behavior.
The selected durable-work RequiredContentVersion does not gate hydration and is not compared to current source state in this service.
Stable metadata with no concrete root/body row is surfaced through the deterministic projection-processing failure path.

Review code to confirm it does not lock DocumentProjectionWork or issue source-row update locks during hydration.

description: Implement descriptor hydration inside the DocumentCache materializer. Resolve descriptor documents by DocumentId and ResourceKeyId from the canonical dms.Document plus dms.Descriptor source, then pass the row through the descriptor cache-projection mode. This path should be internal and caller-agnostic, with no namespace authorization check and no readable-profile projection.
acceptance-criteria: Descriptor materialization starts from the same canonical DocumentId source metadata observation as ordinary resources.
The descriptor row is hydrated from dms.Descriptor for the same DocumentId and expected ResourceKeyId.
A missing descriptor body with stable dms.Document metadata is treated as deterministic projection/source corruption, not as a successful stale suppression.
Descriptor output uses the descriptor cache materialization mode and descriptor StreamEtag context.
The path does not run descriptor namespace authorization or query public descriptor URIs as the materializer source of truth.

description: Add the materializer boundary source-coherence check. The materializer should observe dms.Document metadata before hydration, hydrate the document, then re-read canonical metadata for the same DocumentId and require DocumentUuid, ResourceKeyId, ContentVersion, and ContentLastModifiedAt to match the first observation before returning a candidate.
acceptance-criteria: If the final metadata read finds no dms.Document row, the materializer returns missing-source and no candidate.
If the final metadata read differs in DocumentUuid, ResourceKeyId, ContentVersion, or ContentLastModifiedAt, the materializer returns source-changed and no candidate.
If canonical metadata is stable but the resource/descriptor body cannot be hydrated, the materializer throws the deterministic projection-processing exception required by the story.
The coherence check does not compare current source metadata to the selected durable-work RequiredContentVersion.
The materializer leaves authoritative current source/cache/work classification to the later cache writer story.

Inspect the materializer implementation to confirm no source/cache/work classification logic was added.

description: Implement materializer invariant validation and bounded diagnostics. Before returning success, validate the JSON and metadata invariants owned by DMS-1312. Failures should throw deterministic projection-processing exceptions with bounded sanitized reason metadata, produce no cache candidate, and leave retry/backoff decisions to the caller.
acceptance-criteria: The success path validates that DocumentJson is a JSON object.
The success path validates that DocumentJson.id exactly matches the canonical DocumentUuid string.
The success path validates that DocumentJson._lastModifiedDate exactly matches the existing whole-second UTC formatter applied to ContentLastModifiedAt without rounding.
The success path validates that DocumentJson has no _etag.
The success path validates that StreamEtag equals shared served-ETag composer output for the fixed stream representation.
The success path validates denormalized ProjectName, ResourceName, and ResourceVersion against the selected ResourceKey/read plan.
Invariant failures are not converted into missing-source or source-changed outcomes.
Invariant diagnostics include bounded reason codes and sanitized target/document/resource metadata without logging full DocumentJson or authorization data.

This is a correctness fix for coherent single-document materialization, not a request to add target discovery, lifecycle validation, replacement supervision, durable-work orchestration, cache writes, or Kafka behavior to DMS-1312.
